ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Muscle will contract when stimulated, and the changes in electric potential inside and outside the muscle cell membrane before and after the muscle is stimulated are the same as the potential changes in nerve fibers. Now take two fresh nerve-muscle specimens, and place the nerve of the left specimen on the muscle of the right specimen; at this time the nerve fiber is connected with the muscle cell (during the experiment the specimens are moistened with physiological saline), as shown in the figure. In the figure, ② and ④ refer to the junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells; these junctions are similar to synaptic structures. Stimulating ① can cause the right muscle to contract, and the left muscle also contracts along with it. Among ①, ②, ③, and ④, which ones can carry out excitation transmission (write the labels)?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Muscle will contract when stimulated, and the changes in electric potential inside and outside the muscle cell membrane before and after the muscle is stimulated are the same as the potential changes in nerve fibers. Now take two fresh nerve-muscle specimens, and place the nerve of the left specimen on the muscle of the right specimen; at this time the nerve fiber is connected with the muscle cell (during the experiment the specimens are moistened with physiological saline), as shown in the figure. In the figure, ② and ④ refer to the junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells; these junctions are similar to synaptic structures. Stimulating ① can cause the right muscle to contract, and the left muscle also contracts along with it. Among ①, ②, ③, and ④, which ones can carry out excitation transmission (write the labels)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there are left and right nerve-muscle specimens. The right muscle of the right specimen is connected to a nerve fiber segment labeled “nerve”; ① is located on the right nerve, and an arrow labeled “S stimulation” points to this place; ② is located at the place where the right nerve contacts the right muscle. The left muscle of the left specimen is also connected to a nerve; the left nerve is placed horizontally over the right muscle, ③ is labeled on this nerve fiber itself, and ④ is located at the place where the left nerve contacts the left muscle. Then reason: The question stem clearly states that ② and ④ are junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells, and these junctions are similar to synaptic structures. In biology, “excitation transmission” usually refers to excitation passing from one cell to another at a synapse-like or nerve-muscle junction; whereas propagation of potential changes on the same nerve fiber or the same muscle cell membrane belongs to excitation conduction, and is not called intercellular excitation transmission. ① is only the stimulation site, not a junction; ③ is a nerve fiber segment, and also not a junction between a nerve fiber and a muscle cell. ② and ④ are nerve-muscle junctions and can carry out excitation transmission. Therefore, the answer is ②, ④.
